title: Pagination Label
prompt: A React pagination footer needs a human-readable range. Write a helper that returns "start-end of total" for the current page using 1-based page numbers. If total is 0, return "0-0 of 0".

explanation.beginner:
Example: paginationLabel(1, 10, 35) produces "1-10 of 35". Map each explicitly supported state to its exact output text or value. Separate state selection from formatting.

Compare “labels a partial final page”: input [4,10,35] produces "31-35 of 35". Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Map each explicitly supported state to its exact output text or value. Separate state selection from formatting.

Tempting mistake: Capitalization, whitespace, and boolean-versus-string output are part of the contract; truthiness alone may combine distinct states.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “labels a partial final page”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
